title: The Sun and the Solar System
seo_title: Grade 9 Science (SNC1W): The Sun and the Solar System Worksheets (Ontario)
short_title: the Sun and the solar system
standard_text: The characteristics of the Sun and its importance to the solar system and to life on Earth; how the Sun's energy drives natural phenomena and renewable energy; the major components of the solar system; and the causes of phenomena observed from Earth (day and night, seasons, phases of the Moon, eclipses). (summary of The Ontario Curriculum, Science, Grade 9: SNC1W (2022), Strand E: Space Exploration)
meta_desc: Free Grade 9 Science (SNC1W) worksheets on the Sun and the solar system: the Sun's layers and energy, sunspots, the planets, seasons, phases of the Moon, eclipses and orbits. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The Sun makes energy by nuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium.
key_sub: Seasons are caused by Earth's tilt, not its distance from the Sun.
body_html:
How to think about it

The Sun is a medium-sized star made mostly of hydrogen and helium. In its core, fusion turns hydrogen into helium and releases huge amounts of energy, which travels out as light and heat. Sunspots, solar flares and the solar wind can cause auroras and disturb satellites. The Sun's energy drives weather, the water cycle, photosynthesis, wind and solar power.

The solar system has eight planets: four rocky inner planets and four gas and ice giants, plus dwarf planets, moons, asteroids and comets. Earth's tilt of 23.5° causes the seasons; the Moon's phases come from how much of its sunlit half we see; eclipses happen when the Sun, Earth and Moon line up.

Example

Why is it summer in Canada in July?

The Northern Hemisphere tilts towards the Sun.

Answer: sunlight is more direct and days are longer

Example

Which phase of the Moon happens during a solar eclipse?

The Moon is between the Sun and Earth.

Answer: new moon

Common mistakes

  • Saying the seasons come from Earth being closer to the Sun.
  • Thinking the Moon makes its own light.
  • Calling the Sun a planet or the biggest star.

faq.a: Charged particles from the Sun hit gases in the upper atmosphere near the poles and make them glow.

faq.q: Why can't we have a solar eclipse every month?
faq.a: The Moon's orbit is tilted about 5°, so it usually passes above or below the line from the Sun to Earth.

items.q: What causes the seasons on Earth?
c: the tilt of the Earth's axis as it orbits the Sun
the Earth's changing distance from the Sun
items.e: The Earth's axis is tilted at about 23.5°.

items.q: It is December. Ethan lives in the Southern Hemisphere. Which season is it there?
items.e: The hemisphere tilted toward the Sun has summer; the seasons are opposite in the two hemispheres.

items.q: It is June. How high is the noon Sun in the sky where Ethan lives in the Northern Hemisphere, compared with the rest of the year?
c: exactly overhead every day of the year
lower than at any other time of year
higher than at any other time of year
items.e: The tilt toward the Sun makes the noon Sun higher in summer and lower in winter.
